name: Rufous-winged Illadopsis
rangeDescription: Senegal to ghana; single record from togo
description: A mid-sized, chunky, drably colored babbler. Has a white throat and pale gray underparts, often with some darker olive-brown on the breast.

name: Drakensberg Siskin
rangeDescription: Montane scrub of western kwazulu-natal and lesotho (drakensberg mountains)
description: A small, flighty, brown-lemon siskin of high-elevation grassland and shrubland above 2000 meters of elevation; partial to rocky outcrops. The lemon rump, visible in flight, and the white outer tail feathers most easily identify it.

name: Yucatan Nightjar
rangeDescription: Yucatán peninsula and cozumel; winters to belize and northern honduras
description: Fairly large dark nightjar of woodland, edge, and adjacent clearings in the Yucatan Peninsula. Hunts mainly from perches at forest edge, sometimes even on fence posts in rather open areas.

name: Buff-crested Bustard
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan to eastern ethiopia, djibouti, and somalia to northeastern uganda, kenya, and north-central tanzania
description: A fairly small bustard of thick brush in dry country. The male has a buff crest that is usually hidden, and both sexes have a black belly.

name: Cherrie's Antwren
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia, southwestern venezuela, northeastern peru, and northwestern brazil
description: Heavily streaked antwren. Males are black and white, while females are buff with black streaks.

name: Bacan Myzomela
rangeDescription: Bacan (northern moluccas)
description: A small honeyeater with a short, downcurved bill. Striking male shows a scarlet head, back, and rump, a contrastingly dark tail and wings, and a whitish belly.

name: Black-capped Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of costa rica to western colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: Tiny short-tailed flycatcher, one of the smallest songbirds in the world. Similar shape and size to a golf ball.

name: Rock Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Central and southern minas gerais, brazil
description: A small mostly gray tapaculo with brown and rusty streaks on the belly and vent. The tail is short and usually held cocked.

name: Bronze-winged Courser
rangeDescription: Open woodland of sub-saharan africa
description: Large courser with dark brown upperparts and a white belly. In flight, shows a dark upperwing and a black-and-white underwing.

name: Blue-eyed Cockatoo
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A large, bulky white parrot with a tall yellow-and-white crest that it often raises when perched and bright blue skin around the eyes. In flight, underwing and undertail washed yellowish.

name: Sulawesi Honey-buzzard
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including togian, banggai, and sula islands (off eastern sulawesi) and muna and buton (to southeast)
description: A small-headed, long-tailed raptor from Sulawesi and the Banggai Islands. Adult shows a dark crested head, a pale throat with dark central stripe, a rufous breast with bold streaking, and a barred belly.

name: Green Indigobird
rangeDescription: Locally in zambia, southwestern tanzania, malawi, and zimbabwe
description: Nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of Peters’s Twinspot. Breeding males are glossy greenish-black, and in good light may show a paler gray wash across the head and breast.

name: Kashmir Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india (kashmir); winters to southern india and sri lanka
description: Stubby little flycatcher with a highly restricted range; breeds in a corner of the northwestern Himalayas and winters in isolated pockets of hill forest in southern India and Sri Lanka. Male is gray above and bright orange below; female is paler, with only a faint orange wash on the chest.

name: Bare-cheeked Trogon
rangeDescription: Lowland rainforest of cameroon, gabon, and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A trogon of lowland rainforests, almost always found in the forest interior, away from forest edges. Males and females have distinctive bare yellow facial skin below their eyes and between their eyes and bill.

name: Northern Cassowary
rangeDescription: Lowlands of new guinea, including raja ampat islands (off western new guinea) and yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: An enormous flightless bird of lowland rainforest. Shaggy black plumage, blue head and bright red or yellow around the base of the neck.

name: Common Sunbird-Asity
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern madagascar
description: Tiny, round, short-tailed bird with a long curved bill. Breeding males are blue on the back and yellow below, with bright bare skin around the eye.

name: Andean Slaty Thrush
rangeDescription: Breeds in the andes of southern bolivia (north to santa cruz) and northwestern argentina (southward to córdoba), also locally in southwestern ecuador and northwestern peru; nonbreeding migrant to the east slope of the andes from southeastern ecuador to bolivia
description: A distinctive gray thrush found in montane forests below around 2,000 m from Peru to Argentina. Males are medium-gray above and paler gray below with a darker head, lightly streaked throat, and a yellow bill and eyering.

name: Scaly Weaver
rangeDescription: Southwestern angola, namibia, far southern zambia, botswana, zimbabwe, and northern and central south africa
description: A very small, sandy-colored finch-like weaver with a scaly crown, a pale pink bill, and a black moustache on a white throat that gives it a fierce-looking expression. Small groups are resident and nomadic in grassy arid savanna, where there are trees and scrub nearby in which to build their untidy oval grass nests.

name: Mindoro Bulbul
rangeDescription: Philippines (mindoro and semirara)
description: A medium-sized bird of lowland and montane forest and more open wooded areas on Mindoro and Semirara. Dark brown on the upperparts and chest with a pale belly, a fairly long stout black bill, and a grayish head with faint streaks.

name: Jabiru
rangeDescription: West-central mexico through south america to northeastern argentina
description: Huge, massive-billed, and unmistakable stork of tropical lowlands. Found in marshes and flooded fields, but nests high in large trees.
